_comment: SHOSMED physics, SECOND 60-question block. Implemented 19 November 2026 from
SHOSMED_Physics_Batch2_Review_and_Claude_Prompt.txt.
HOW THE IDS WERE VERIFIED. The review supplied ORIGINAL IDENTIFICATION
SIGNATURES and explicitly warned against assuming phys-61..phys-120,
contiguity or zero overlap, so the map was derived by FULL CONTENT MATCH of
each original stem plus all four original option texts against all 280
physics records, on a canonical form that decodes named HTML entities,
strips tags, folds sub/superscripts to plain digits and normalises dashes,
Greek letters, arrows and whitespace.
- 56 matched exactly. The remaining 4 (Q1, Q5, Q44, Q58) matched only once
whitespace was ignored entirely: those are exactly the items the review
flags for typography checking, and their stored OPTION texts carry <sup>
markup that the export flattened into line breaks inside the exponents.
No stored record was wrong.
- No two of the 280 records share a signature under either form, so no
match was ambiguous and none needed the explanation as a tie-break.
- Every stored topic equalled the signature topic.
- All 60 stored answer letters equalled the review key block, and the
review changes no letter, so NO key was changed and there is no
disagreement to report. The tally stays A=6, B=28, C=26, D=0.
The block turns out to be phys-61 .. phys-120 in display order, contiguous,
but that is a RESULT of the matching rather than the assumption the review
warned against. It does not overlap the previously reviewed 60, so all 60 are
newly reviewed ids.
DISTRACTOR FEEDBACK. None of the 60 stored explanations carried any: the
block has no "Why the other choices are wrong" heading and no lettered
feedback paragraph anywhere, so the 180 added here duplicate nothing. The
markup follows the convention of the physics records that already carry
feedback (phys-226 .. phys-250), and each heading is derived from that
item's own stored option text, so a renamed option carries its new text into
its heading automatically. Feedback is placed after the main explanation and
before the Key Concept, as the review directs.
STRUCTURE AS STORED, checked rather than assumed: this block has NO tables,
no Key Educational Points block, no Bottom Line and no div, every item has
exactly one Key Concept, and nothing follows that Key Concept. All 60 keyed
headings are UNLETTERED, so that convention is preserved throughout.
TYPOGRAPHY. Q1, Q5, Q44 and Q58 already store correct <sup> markup with real
U+2212 minus signs, and Q52 already stores "3.34 × 10<sup>5</sup> J/kg", so
the flattened appearances in the export were extraction artifacts and no
markup was changed for them. The block stores no HTML entity, no em dash and
no curly quote, and none was introduced.

notes: The review's own inventory was cross-checked and closes: the displays touched by a stem, main-explanation, Key Concept or option change leave exactly the twelve the review lists as core-content-kept (Q1, Q2, Q4, Q11, Q12, Q15, Q17, Q20, Q28, Q43, Q47, Q49).
The four Key-Concept-only items (Q3, Q6, Q30, Q50) appear in the Key Concept list and in none of the stem or main lists, as the review describes.
Q56's correction changes an option's text, not its letter: C stays the keyed answer and its keyed heading is re-synchronized to 26.3°C.
'Unanswered' and 'Report an issue' appear in no stored field anywhere in the physics bank, so they are interface text and are not counted as content corrections.
No answer letter, id, topic or subject moved, and no answer-position rebalancing was done.
Structural and consistency checks establish scope and presentation. They do not establish scientific accuracy, which rests on the content review itself.
